title: Credit Line Increase Calculation for Northgate Card Accounts — Credit Risk Standard
content:
**When an increase is granted.** These standards govern requested credit line increases on **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** accounts. A requested credit line increase is granted only after the minimum payment due on the statement for which the most recent late fee was recorded, the missed statement, is met in full by the payments recorded against that statement that were not returned unpaid.

The minimum payment due on that statement is the minimum printed on it, less the amount the base rule excludes while a billing-error dispute stands open: where exactly one billing-error dispute is recorded on a transaction that statement first showed, it still stands open with no resolution entry referring back to it and its notice was received after that statement's closing date, the minimum payment due is worked out in two steps, first the tier's minimum payment percentage of the disputed amount, rounded half up to the cent, is taken off the printed minimum, then where what remains is below the tier's minimum payment floor the floor is used instead, never more than the printed minimum; in every other case the minimum payment due is the printed minimum.

A payment is recorded against the statement whose balance it pays, and a returned payment against the same statement as the payment it returns; where two late fees posted the same day, the most recent late fee is the one entered first in the account history, and while the increase is not granted the credit limit stays as it is.

**Referral.** A requested credit line increase is not granted, and is referred to the disputes team, while the statement for which the most recent late fee was recorded carries two or more billing-error disputes on transactions it first showed, whether resolved or not: no limit change is booked and the customer is handed over to a human representative because no published policy decides the increase in this conversation.

**The new limit.** The line increase is taken at 10 percent of the account's current credit limit, and the new credit limit is the current credit limit plus the line increase, rounded down to a whole hundred dollars (in steps of 100 dollars) and never above the tier's highest credit limit. Every line addition is added to the current credit limit together with the line increase before the rounding down to a whole hundred dollars and the tier ceiling.

## Worked figures (hypothetical accounts)

| Current credit limit | Line increase at 10 percent | Sum | Rounded down to a whole hundred | Tier's highest credit limit | New credit limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1750.00 | 175.00 | 1925.00 | 1900.00 | 10000.00 | 1900.00 |
| 2480.00 | 248.00 | 2728.00 | 2700.00 | 2500.00 | 2500.00 |

**Minimum payment due, worked.** A missed statement printed a minimum of 58.00; exactly one billing-error dispute of 900.00, still open, is recorded on a transaction it first showed, with the notice received after its closing date; on a tier with a 1 percent minimum payment percentage and a 40.00 floor, 1 percent of 900.00 is 9.00, and 58.00 less 9.00 leaves 49.00, above the floor and not more than 58.00, so the minimum payment due is 49.00. Payments of 49.00 recorded against that statement, none returned unpaid, meet it; payments of 60.00 of which 30.00 was returned unpaid leave 30.00, which does not.
